presence.registered: The instruction type and wire id are in the registry and a handler exists. Nothing else.
presence.carrier: No instruction; the operation travels as an executable variant, a syscall sequence, a block artifact or a Torii route.
presence.absent: No instruction or other carrier exists. `carrier.registry_pattern` makes the check fail when one is added.

verification.implemented: A native verifier of the named relation is compiled and this operation reaches it: the recorded `verifier_path` (by default the handler) names the verifier, link by link. `test_evidence` says whether a cited test that runs by default calls it. Not a soundness, zero-knowledge or qualification claim.
verification.binding_only: Only public-data binding is verified; no private-witness relation.
verification.signature_only: A signature stands where the plan requires a proof.
verification.refused: The operation always returns the recorded typed refusal before any proof is accepted.
verification.not_applicable: The operation carries no proof (an administrative or plain state transition).

state_effects.implemented: The handler applies its effect when its checks pass.
state_effects.gated: The effect exists and is behind an activation, qualification or node-configured prerequisite the plan removes.
state_effects.unreachable: The handler refuses before the effect, for every input.
state_effects.none: Verification only; nothing is written that later validity depends on.

delivery.not_delivered: The operation-v1 delivery of the plan (typed instruction, Kotodama binding, one-call and prepared SDK operation in six families, fixtures, real proof and effect, four validators, restart and replay) is incomplete; `missing` says what.
delivery.delivered: Allowed only when every owning task is `implemented` in specs/zk_delivery_graph.json.

relation_status.implemented: Compiled verifier. `test_evidence` says whether a cited test that runs by default calls it.

test_anchors.default: A `path` and `test` pair names a test that carries `#[test]`, is not `#[ignore]`d and is compiled by the crate's default features.
test_anchors.ignored: `ignored: true` marks a test that exists and is `#[ignore]`d. It counts as `not_default` evidence only.
test_anchors.feature: `feature` names the Cargo feature, outside the crate's defaults, that gates the test's file or top-level module. It counts as `not_default` evidence only.
test_anchors.covers: `covers` marks a cited test that is not evidence for the verifier (a preflight, a table check, a no-proof fixture, a refusal before the verifier) and says what it shows. It is never counted toward `test_evidence`.
test_anchors.reaches: `reaches` lists the functions or `impl` blocks, in other files, through which a cited test gets to the verifier. The checker requires each to name the next.

test_evidence.default: At least one cited test that runs by default names the verifier, a function on the recorded path to it, or reaches one through its `reaches` links.
test_evidence.not_default: Only cited tests that are `#[ignore]`d or feature-gated do. `test_note` says what the default run covers.
test_evidence.none: No cited test does. `test_note` says what the cited tests cover instead.
test_evidence.limit: Reach is textual: the names are in the test (or in a function it calls in its file, or in the functions its `reaches` list names). It shows the test is about the verifier, not that the call runs or that a valid proof is accepted.

registry.what: Every built-in instruction and its wire id. A module is the last path segment before the type name; instructions declared at the top of the registry have the empty module.

authority.what: How the authority checks of a handler are found. The handler is its `impl Execute` block together with the other trait impls of the instruction type in the same file. authority.limit: Reading is textual and stops at the handler's own blocks.
